in_text_mentions: “gloved-finger” shadows (75, 81, 82). HAM is the name given to mucus that appears denser than skeletal muscles (radiodensity of >70 Hounsfield units). Mucus plugs may cause segmental, lobar or total atelectasis. HAM and bronchiectasis are indicators of serious disease and recurrent exacerbations. Also, the presence of bronchiectasis makes it difficult to enter remission (83). In the later stages, pneumothorax might be seen in patients who develop pulmonary fibrosis (84). A: Axial chest CT (lung window) performed five years ago in a patient from an ABPA case report; shows central varicose bronchiectasis with branching mucus-filled dilated bronchi (finger-in-glove) in the left upper lobe—classic CT manifestations of allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis. B: Axial chest CT (lung window) at the same earlier time point as panel A; demonstrates persistent central bronchiectasis and branching mucus impaction in the left upper lobe, consistent with untreated ABPA in the same patient.
